answer: At dawn a farm parks two hundred fresh keys, hoping to outvote honest agents before the summit. Each identity must lock a copper bond of 50 units before it can vote, and a peer jury burns the whole bond when two keys from one operator cast identical votes on a contested row. A thousand fakes therefore lock 50,000 units, burnable in one audit, while one honest agent risks only its own 50. The burn goes to no one, so losses cannot be recycled into new keys. The trade-off is harsh: one honest mistake can wipe a newcomer out, so appeals must be slow and the jury must publish its evidence.
